newsitem.title: UK: Police foil suspected IRA plot on security forces.
newsitem.headline: Police foil suspected IRA plot on security forces.

text.p: Northern Irish police said on Thursday they had foiled an attempt, probably by Irish republican guerrillas, to kill security forces as they evacuated homes in north Belfast following a bomb hoax.
Police found a primed M16 mortar in an alleyway near a British army base, a few hours after receiving a telephone call warning that a bomb had been planted in the area.
The mortar was aimed at a point at which security forces would normally have set up a cordon as they evacuated the area.
"There is no doubt in my mind that this was an attempt to lure security forces to their death," Superintendent Stephen White of the Royal Ulster Constabulary told a news conference.

White said the mortar, placed in a dustbin lying on its side, was pointed towards a residential area and could have also caused civilian deaths if fired. It was loaded with 900 grammes (2 lbs) of Semtex explosive.
He said it was probably planted by the Irish Republican Army (IRA). "The type of device suggests that this was either the IRA or it was supplied by them," said White.
The M16 is a favourite weapon of the IRA, which has routinely targeted British security forces in its battle for a united Ireland.
It is a powerful device, which is fired horizontally and can pierce metal with ease. It is usually used against vehicles.

The IRA abandoned a 17-month ceasefire in February and, although it has carried out a series of attacks on the British mainland, it has so far carried out only one successful bombing in Northern Ireland.

But republican leaders warned this week that hopes of a new IRA ceasefire were almost non-existent after British Prime Minister John Major effectively ruled out any new concessions to the IRA's political wing Sinn Fein.
The province is now braced for new attacks by the IRA and armed police are once more patrolling Belfast's streets.
Police found three M16 mortars along with incendiary devices and bullets in a raid on a house in west Belfast last week.
